description: Both commit-path and recovery trim audits converge: Metadata's eleven structured slots have ZERO production readers - only .version is consumed (ack) - while FDB's txnStateStore is a plain KV store (ApplyMetadataMutation.cpp:238 txnStateStore->set(KeyValueRef(m.param1,m.param2))) with parsed views only where consumers exist; Bedrock's consumer-facing view is RoutingData, built in the same window-apply step. Collapse Metadata to {version} + skip-count telemetry (~30 lines): deletes family_of, 20 put/delete_entry clauses, known_entries and ~25 reverse key-reconstruction functions duplicating SystemKeys backwards, clear_range parallel bookkeeping (a divergence hazard class in itself), Values decode coupling, stats plumbing. ~230 prod lines + most of metadata_test.exs. q67.9/q67.23's reader rebuilds the structured view WITH its reader, shaped by what the reader needs - the doctrine's txnStateStore analogue arrives with its consumer, not before.
title: Trim: CommitProxy.Metadata collapses to a version tracker
